title: Where the growth in spending went
question: Of the $465 million more a year the district spends than in fiscal 2015, which kinds of spending took it?
finding: Instruction took 65% of the $465 million growth in day-to-day spending between fiscal 2015 and fiscal 2024 ($404 million to $707 million). The fastest-growing line was business, central and other support services, +146% ($25.5 million to $62.9 million). Support for teaching staff fell $35.9 million; Construction and other capital spending fell $111 million. Long-term debt outstanding was $781 million at the end of fiscal 2015 and $933 million at the end of fiscal 2024.
how: The federal survey's own spending categories, for the district and county office together, fiscal 2015 and 2024. The ten day-to-day categories add up to total day-to-day spending; "other support services" is what is left of the support-services total after its seven named lines. "General administration" and "business, central and other support services" are the survey's two central-office categories. Per-pupil figures use the all-San-Francisco pupil count.
limits: How a district codes a cost to a category is its own choice within State accounting rules, and San Francisco changed which of its two reporting units carried transport and special-education costs during these years; adding the two units removes that, but a shift between categories would still show as growth in one and a fall in another. Construction spending follows bond programmes and swings from year to year. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation. A district where living costs are high must pay more to hire and keep staff, and one with many small schools, or with many pupils who are learning English, have disabilities or are poor, will spend more per pupil for honest reasons; none of those is measured here.
